Description: powerhint.json for TECNO CM6 (MediaTek mt6789) with AOSP android.hardware.power-service.pixel-libperfmgr.
This file is authored from THIS device's own data, not copied from any other device tree.
Sources of truth:
* Live sysfs OPP tables read from the running device (policy0/policy6/dvfsrc/ged).
* Stock vendor power config vendor/etc/powercontable.xml (decrypted) - resource paths, bounds, defaults.
* Stock vendor power config vendor/etc/powerscntbl.xml (decrypted) - stock hint->resource policy.
* Stock boot logcat - confirms cluster topology, dvfsrc OPP list, GED level count.
Parsed by hardware/google/pixel/power-libperfmgr/libperfmgr/HintManager.cc.
Rules the parser enforces (violation => GetInstance()==nullptr => LOG(FATAL) 'Invalid config'):
* Node Name and Path must be unique across all Nodes.
* Values must be non-empty, unique within a Node; a File node value may not be empty.
* DefaultIndex must be < Values.size(). If omitted the parser falls back to the LAST index.
* Every Node-type Action needs PowerHint, Node, Value (member of that Node's Values) and Duration (UInt64).
* A given Node may appear at most once inside a single PowerHint.
* Hints that are not listed here are safely ignored by DoHint()/EndHint().
CRITICAL - Values ORDER is significant. FileNode::Update() walks req_sorted_ from index 0 and
applies the FIRST index with an active request; req_sorted_ preserves the JSON Values order
verbatim (HintManager.cc does NOT sort). Therefore:
* MIN / floor nodes (CPULittleMinFreq, CPUBigMinFreq, MemFreq, TopAppUclampMin,
latency_sensitive, GED timer margin, GPU boost/min, sugov rate limits) MUST list the HIGHEST /
most-aggressive value FIRST (descending) and the release value LAST (usually DefaultIndex).
* MAX / cap nodes (CPULittleMaxFreq, CPUBigMaxFreq, GpuMaxFreq) MUST list the MOST-restrictive
value FIRST (ascending freq). The Pixel thermal HAL (powerhal_helper.cpp setMode->DoHint) is
CUMULATIVE (it enables every severity <= current), so ascending is what makes the worst active
severity win; reversing max nodes would break thermal throttling.

Nodes.Name: CPULittleMinFreq
Comments: policy0 = CPUs 0-5, 6x Cortex-A55. Measured OPPs (kHz):
Ordered HIGHEST-first (descending) on purpose: FileNode::Update() picks the FIRST req_sorted_
index with an active request, so the highest active floor wins. The LAST index '0' == release
the floor (kernel clamps to cpuinfo_min 500000); DefaultIndex 5 == that. This is the same
release convention the device uses in rootdir/etc/init.cgroup.rc (scaling_min_freq 0).
Boost points 1000000/1300000/1500000/1700000/2000000 are all real OPPs and mirror the
stock powerscntbl.xml values (IN_LAUNCHER 1300000, UX_SCROLLING 1500000, WHITELIST_LAUNCH 2000000).

Nodes.Name: CPUBigMinFreq
Comments: policy6 = CPUs 6-7, 2x Cortex-A76. Measured OPPs (kHz):
Ordered HIGHEST-first (descending); LAST index '0' == release, DefaultIndex 7 == that.
Kernel clamps to cpuinfo_min 725000.
Boost points mirror stock powerscntbl.xml (IN_LAUNCHER 1800000, WHITELIST_LAUNCH 2200000).

Nodes.Name: CPULittleMaxFreq
Comments: Cap node for policy0. Ordered MOST-restrictive-first (ascending freq) on purpose:
libperfmgr FileNode::Update() picks the FIRST req_sorted_ index with an active
request, so with ascending order the lowest (= most restrictive) active cap wins.
This is required for the cumulative THERMAL_ap_ntc_* hints (the thermal HAL enables
every severity <= current). DefaultIndex 6 = 2000000 == cpuinfo_max, i.e. no cap.
All values are real policy0 OPPs (650000 is the lowest writable cap >= the decoded
stock mtk-skin-control cluster0_min_throttle_freq floor), matching power_profile cluster0.

Nodes.Name: CPUBigMaxFreq
Comments: Cap node for policy6. Ordered MOST-restrictive-first (ascending freq): see CPULittleMaxFreq.
DefaultIndex 6 = 2200000 == cpuinfo_max, i.e. no cap.
Value 800000 is the decoded stock mtk-skin-control cluster1_min_throttle_freq floor.

Nodes.Name: TopAppUclampMin
Comments: Stock powercontable.xml PERF_RES_SCHED_UCLAMP_MIN_TA: range 0..100, default 0.
Ordered HIGHEST-first (descending) so the strongest active floor wins.
Stock uses 25 (UX_MOVE_SCROLLING), 40 (UX_SCROLLING), 100 (APP_ROTATE/PMS_INSTALL).

Nodes.Name: TopAppLatencySensitive
Comments: Stock powercontable.xml PERF_RES_SCHED_PREFER_IDLE_TA: range 0..1, default 0.
Stock sets this to 1 for LAUNCH / scroll / game scenarios.

Nodes.Name: ForegroundLatencySensitive
Comments: Stock powercontable.xml PERF_RES_SCHED_PREFER_IDLE_FG: range 0..1, default 0.

Nodes.Name: GedTimerMargin
Comments: Stock powercontable.xml PERF_RES_GPU_GED_TIMER_BASE_DVFS_MARGIN: path timer_base_dvfs_margin.
Live kernel idle value on this device is 30; stock powerscntbl.xml IN_LAUNCHER sets 50.
Ordered HIGHEST-first (descending); higher margin = more aggressive GPU DVFS ramp.

Nodes.Name: GedMarginValue
Comments: GED dvfs_margin_value is a mode/value field, not a plain percentage.
30 selects CONFIGURE_MARGIN_MODE with a 30% margin. Values 101..199 select dynamic CONFIG_FPS margin mode; 201..299 fixed-FPS; 301..399 no-FPS; 401..499 extend; 501..599 perf.
30 is the generic kernel/constant-margin default. No stock app- or game-specific dynamic mode is imported.

Nodes.Name: GedLoadingStep
Comments: Stock powercontable.xml PERF_RES_GPU_GED_LOADING_BASE_DVFS_STEP: path loading_base_dvfs_step, default 4.
Neutral AOSP initialization only; stock game-profile loading-step values are not imported.
The node displays its value in hexadecimal (16 decimal reads back as 10).

Nodes.Name: GedLoadingMode
Comments: Stock powercontable.xml PERF_RES_GPU_GED_DVFS_LOADING_MODE: path dvfs_loading_mode, default 0.
Neutral AOSP initialization only; no game-specific loading policy is imported.

Nodes.Name: GedWorkloadMode
Comments: Stock GED DVFS workload mode: path dvfs_workload_mode, kernel default 0.
Neutral AOSP initialization only; no app- or game-specific workload policy is imported.

Nodes.Name: GpuBoostLevel
Comments: Stock powercontable.xml PERF_RES_GPU_BLOCK_API_BOOST: path gpu_boost_level, range -1..100, default -1.
Ordered HIGHEST-first (descending). -1 == default (GED owns DVFS). 100 == maximum API boost.
Only the strongest GPU hints request 100.

Nodes.Name: GpuMinFreq
Comments: Stock powercontable.xml PERF_RES_GPU_FREQ_MIN: path custom_boost_gpu_freq (GED custom min-floor).
Verified from stock ged.ko: custom_boost_gpu_freq_store() => scnprintf + kstrtoint => mtk_custom_boost_gpu_freq(int level).
So the node takes a SINGLE integer level index (write path is plain %d in vendor libpowerhal.so
set_gpu_freq_level(), which writes /sys/kernel/ged/hal/custom_boost_gpu_freq with snprintf('%d', level)).
Range is 0..total_gpu_freq_level_count-1 (live count=45 => 0..44) and LOWER index == HIGHER frequency
(live current_freqency: level 8 = 990000, level 9 = 976000).
Boost is level 20 (higher freq); release is level 44 == lowest freq (kernel idle value).
Ordered most-aggressive-first so the higher floor wins; DefaultIndex 1 == '44' == release.
Stock powerscntbl.xml IN_LAUNCHER sets PERF_RES_GPU_FREQ_MIN=20 => floor the GPU at level 20.

Nodes.Name: GpuMaxFreq
Comments: GED DVFS ceiling (custom_upbound_gpu_freq) - the max-freq counterpart of GpuMinFreq.
Same level-index ABI as custom_boost_gpu_freq: LOWER index == HIGHER frequency, so
index 0 == highest OPP == no ceiling. Verified live on this device: while
custom_upbound_gpu_freq=0 the GPU still runs at level 9 (976 MHz), i.e. 0 does NOT
force a low clock. Write test: '20' => stored value '20', restored to '0'.
Values are ordered MOST-RESTRICTIVE-FIRST (lowest freq / highest index first) on
purpose: FileNode::Update() picks the FIRST req_sorted_ index with an active request,
so the most restrictive active cap wins (same rule as CPULittleMaxFreq).
DefaultIndex 4 == '0' == no cap. Stock app-cfg PERF_RES_GPU_FREQ_MAX values: 8,9,26,29.

Nodes.Name: GpuThermalLimit
Comments: gpufreqv2 THERMAL_AP limiter (id 2, priority 7); higher priority than POWERHAL (id 10, priority 4).
The THERMAL_AP set path takes FREQUENCY in kHz, not an OPP index. The kernel maps it to the closest OPP.
390000=44/390MHz, 733000=29/733MHz, 835000=20/835MHz; 0 cancels the thermal ceiling.
Floor is -2 (GPUPPM_KEEP_IDX), so this cap does not erase the power-HAL game floor.
The THERMAL_AP row is enabled at boot. Do not use 'switch 2 0 0' here because a later set would leave it disabled.
Values are ordered most-restrictive-first for cumulative thermal hints; DefaultIndex 3 == no cap.

Nodes.Name: SugovLittleUpRateLimit
Comments: Stock powercontable.xml PERF_RES_SCHED_UTIL_UP_RATE_LIMIT_US_CLUSTER_0.
policy0 runs the MTK sugov_ext governor. Stock powerscntbl.xml UX_SCROLLING_COMMON_MODE
writes 0 (uncapped up-ramp => governor may raise freq immediately). Live boot value is 1.

Nodes.Name: SugovLittleDownRateLimit
Comments: Stock powercontable.xml PERF_RES_SCHED_UTIL_DOWN_RATE_LIMIT_US_CLUSTER_0.
0 == uncapped down-ramp (stock UX_SCROLLING_COMMON_MODE). Live boot value is 1.

Nodes.Name: SugovBigUpRateLimit
Comments: Stock powercontable.xml PERF_RES_SCHED_UTIL_UP_RATE_LIMIT_US_CLUSTER_1.
policy6 runs the MTK sugov_ext governor. Live boot value is 1.

Nodes.Name: SugovBigDownRateLimit
Comments: Stock powercontable.xml PERF_RES_SCHED_UTIL_DOWN_RATE_LIMIT_US_CLUSTER_1.
policy6 runs the MTK sugov_ext governor. Live boot value is 1.

Nodes.Name: MemFreq
Comments: DVFSRC (EMI/DDR) devfreq is on the userspace governor on this device.
2400000000,3200000000,4266000000 -- matches the stock boot log libPowerHal
'get_dvfsrc_devfreq_table count:7'.
Ordered HIGHEST-first (descending) so the highest active floor wins. The LAST index '0'
== release the floor (kernel clamps to min_freq 800000000); DefaultIndex 3 == that.
Stock keeps PERF_RES_DRAM_OPP_MIN=0 (min) for most hints incl. LAUNCH, so no UI hint raises
DDR here (matches stock); only INTERACTION/LAUNCH/EXPENSIVE_RENDERING lift it.

Nodes.Name: TouchGesture
Comments: Transsion FTS gesture enable via the tran_touch proc node (stock path).
Format: '<2-letter gesture code><1-digit 0/1>'. 'cc1' arms double-tap-to-wake
so the driver enters TRAN_GESTURE_SUSPEND_MODE at screen-off and reports
KEY_F26 (linux 198) on a double tap. 'cc0' disarms.
Armed automatically while the PM DOUBLE_TAP_TO_WAKE mode is active
(Settings.Secure.double_tap_to_wake on) and disarmed on EndHint/init.
